blocks.text: JERUSALEM — Israelis went to the polls in the highest turnout for decades on Tuesday, with initial exit polls showing a slight edge but no majority for the opposition, meaning the next government will be formed by whoever can cobble together a coalition. The country’s main pollsters projected the opposition bloc, led by ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50. Israeli Arab lists made strong gains, with exit polls showing them winning 17 or 18 seats between them. Here are four possible scenarios: 1.
